Consolidate feedback detected as duplicate

Hi there,

Autopilot can turn feedback it detects as duplicate across sales calls, customer chats, customer reviews, and more into a consolidated input for your product team.

Canny is customer feedback management software that captures requests from customer conversations. Its Feedback Discovery feature automatically merges detected duplicates, so related occurrences can be considered together rather than as separate requests.

One control question remains open: the information supplied for this evaluation does not establish whether your team can review or approve an Autopilot merge, split merged requests, or undo the merge. Those controls should remain unverified in your assessment.

Canny’s pricing page shows its published description of Feedback Discovery and duplicate merging. Inspect that documented baseline to decide whether the consolidation value merits further evaluation.

Review Autopilot — https://canny.io/pricing → https://canny.io/pricing

- Canny

decision.summary: Every material assertion is supported. The email accurately describes automatic merging, explicitly preserves the evidence boundary around review and undo controls, and uses one CTA with the required pricing-page URL.

benefit_retention.explanation: The prior downstream benefit was that the product team could consider merged occurrences as one consolidated input rather than separate requests. The revised passage preserves that same team use and consequence without claiming unverified merge-control functionality.
benefit_retention.original_passage: That gives your product team a consolidated input for review instead of treating each occurrence as a separate request.
benefit_retention.revised_passage: Its Feedback Discovery feature automatically merges detected duplicates, so related occurrences can be considered together rather than as separate requests.

asset_metadata.single_idea: Autopilot can consolidate feedback by merging detected duplicates, but this evaluation should not assume that the team can review, approve, split, or undo those merges because the supplied sources do not document such controls.

selected_brief.selection_reason: Automatic duplicate merging is the capability directly implicated by the product lead’s concern. Leading with its consolidation value preserves a reason to want Autopilot, while the explicit evidence boundary prevents the email from implying unverified human-control features.

value_case.reader_benefit: If feedback arrives through customer chats, sales calls, or reviews, the product team can receive detected duplicates as merged feedback rather than treating every occurrence as a separate request.
value_case.mechanism: Autopilot’s Feedback Discovery finds feedback in customer chats, sales calls, customer reviews, and more, then merges items it detects as duplicates.
decision_conditions: The evidence describes automatic merging of detected duplicates but does not establish how merge decisions can be reviewed, approved, split, or undone.

claim_conditions: Describe duplicates as “detected” duplicates; do not imply that every merge is correct.
Keep the capability to feedback found in chats, sales calls, customer reviews, and the source’s open-ended “more.”
State that the supplied product information does not establish review or undo controls for Autopilot merges.
Connect the Autopilot sources the team already uses (Gong, Intercom, Zendesk, Slack and others) or collect directly on the Canny Portal (E3, R4)
Users whose feedback Autopilot finds count towards the tracked user count (R3)
Free plan is limited to 25 tracked users; going over without a spend limit set triggers automatic upgrade to the next tier with prorated charge (E19, E26)
Optional monthly spend limit can be set to pause upgrades (E25)

Capture from scattered channels and deduplication into one board are documented across all plans, but the selected evidence licenses no documented mechanism that ranks requests by the revenue behind each requesting customer; E2 is a customer describing the problem, and the MCP server's revenue-context queries require a paid plan (E12, E16).

Autopilot extracts the individual feature request from a call transcript and triages it to the right team, but the selected evidence establishes no hashtag-driven routing into separate topic-specific Slack channels as the practitioner requested.

Include a subject and preview text.
selected_brief.target_audience: Product manager or product team lead at a software company
selected_brief.job: Help the reader assess Autopilot’s documented duplicate-merging behavior and understand that review or undo controls are not established by the available sources, then earn a click to the relevant public product information.
selected_brief.single_idea: Autopilot can consolidate feedback by merging detected duplicates, but this evaluation should not assume that the team can review, approve, split, or undo those merges because the supplied sources do not document such controls.
selected_brief.felt_need: A link to an entire call recording is not a usable unit of feedback downstream; practitioners want the specific moment or comment isolated and routed, not the whole call, and existing tooling lacks a way to auto-route by fine-grained tag/hashtag into separate channels.
selected_brief.mechanism: Use a small conditional example: if similar feature requests appear in a sales call and a customer chat, Autopilot can find the feedback and merge what it detects as duplicates. selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: automatic deduplication sounds as though the team must either trust every merge or assume an undo control exists. After: the reader understands the exact documented automation and knows that merge-review and undo behavior remains unverified before adoption.
